comment: Where a field writes its cataloguing practice down. This steers the research queries; it is not a resolver. Entries carry a 'site' rather than a deep link on purpose -- the same reason vault-wiki's canonical-sources.json does: entry paths are not constructible from a subject name, so the URL is found by search and matched, never guessed. A cluster is a hint, not a gate: an unmatched subject still researches, it just runs unrestricted queries. Clusters were chosen because each has a published standard a practitioner would actually name; a hobby with no published practice is expected to come back thin, and the run should say so rather than pad. Add a cluster when a real run comes back empty, and record which query found nothing.
generic_queries: how to catalogue a {subject} collection best practice

sources.label: Darwin Core (TDWG)
sources.why: The occurrence/taxon field standard everything else in biodiversity maps to.

sources.label: GBIF
sources.why: Shows Darwin Core as actually published, including which fields are in practice mandatory.

sources.label: Audubon Core (TDWG)
sources.why: The media-description half, for specimen photographs.

sources.label: Index Herbariorum
sources.why: Herbarium label and accession conventions.

sources.label: Spectrum (Collections Trust)
sources.why: The collections-management procedure most museums actually run on.

sources.label: CIDOC-CRM
sources.why: The conceptual reference model for cultural heritage; strong on the event/object split.

sources.label: Getty vocabularies (AAT, TGN, ULAN)
sources.why: Controlled vocabularies for object type, place, and maker.

sources.label: Dublin Core (DCMI)
sources.why: The minimum viable descriptive set, and the one most tools speak.

sources.label: MARC 21
sources.why: What a library catalogue record actually contains.

sources.label: BIBFRAME
sources.why: The work/instance/item split, which is the interesting structural idea.

sources.label: ISAD(G) (ICA)
sources.why: Multi-level description: fonds to item, which is the archival answer to hierarchy.

sources.label: DACS (SAA)
sources.why: The US practice, more concrete than ISAD(G) about required elements.

sources.label: PREMIS
sources.why: Preservation and fixity metadata, for anything digitised.

sources.label: Mindat
sources.why: The de facto locality and species database; its record shape is the field's habit.

sources.label: IMA-CNMNC nomenclature
sources.why: The naming authority for mineral species.

sources.label: Paleobiology Database
sources.why: Occurrence records for fossil material.

sources.label: International Code of Nomenclature for Cultivated Plants
sources.why: Cultivar naming, which differs from botanical binomials.

sources.label: RHS Horticultural Database
sources.why: Cultivar records as published.

sources.label: USDA PLANTS
sources.why: Hardiness, distribution, and accepted names.

sources.label: MusicBrainz style guide
sources.why: A worked, opinionated answer to release/recording/work modelling.

sources.label: Discogs database guidelines
sources.why: Physical-copy cataloguing: pressing, matrix, condition.

sources.label: FRBR / RDA
sources.why: The work/expression/manifestation/item distinction these all descend from.

sources.label: Sheldon and comparable grading scales
sources.why: Condition as a published scale rather than an adjective.

sources.label: Scott / Stanley Gibbons catalogue conventions
sources.why: Catalogue numbering as the identity key.

sources.label: schema.org
sources.why: Recipe, HowTo, and Product give a serviceable field list where no domain standard exists.

sources.label: Ravelry pattern data model
sources.why: A large real-world craft catalogue, useful as observed practice.

sources.label: GEDCOM
sources.why: The interchange format every genealogy tool reads; its event model is the useful part.

sources.label: Genealogical Proof Standard (BCG)
sources.why: Evidence and citation practice, which is the half software gets wrong.

sources.label: Dublin Core (DCMI)
sources.why: The fallback minimum descriptive set.

sources.label: schema.org
sources.why: A published field list for most everyday kinds of thing.

sources.label: Wikipedia
sources.why: Last resort, and only for what the field calls things.
